sdk-internal.gate: cargo +{rustfmt_nightly} fmt -p bitwarden-core --check && cargo clippy -q -p bitwarden-core --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -q -p bitwarden-core --all-features

beads.title: Add PlatformClient::heartbeat() returning the current UTC date and time
beads.description:
FILED AGAINST: {sha}
SOURCE: {source}

The Rust CLI (bwcli-rs) is adding `bw heartbeat`, which prints the current date and time. The time must come from
the SDK, so the CLI exercises a real SDK call. This bead is the SDK half: a public heartbeat method on bitwarden-core
that returns the current date and time to the caller.

Where it fits: `client.platform()` (crates/bitwarden-core/src/platform/platform_client.rs) already hosts small
utility calls such as `fingerprint`, so `client.platform().heartbeat()` is the natural home. Return a
`chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>` (chrono is already a bitwarden-core dependency). It needs no login, network or state.

Consumer: bwcli-rs bead (filed next) waits on this one and calls the method once it is verified on origin/main.

Out of scope: uniffi/wasm bindings, any other crate, changes to existing PlatformClient methods.
beads.acceptance:
- `grep -n "pub fn heartbeat" crates/bitwarden-core/src/platform/platform_client.rs` shows a public `heartbeat` method on `PlatformClient` returning `chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>`
- a unit test in bitwarden-core asserts the returned time is no earlier than a `Utc::now()` taken before the call and no later than one taken after it
- the gate passes: `{gate}`
- `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` lists files under `crates/bitwarden-core/` only

beads.title: Add bw heartbeat: print the current date and time from the SDK
beads.description:
FILED AGAINST: {sha}
SOURCE: {source}
WAITS-ON sdk-internal:{sdk-internal} (verified on sdk-internal origin/main, and the ../sdk-internal checkout is at that commit)

Add a `heartbeat` command: `bw heartbeat` prints the current date and time, obtained from the SDK's
`client.platform().heartbeat()` (added by {sdk-internal}), not computed in the CLI. It exists to prove a change can flow
from the SDK to the CLI.

Where it fits: a new variant in `Commands` (crates/bw-cli/src/main.rs) with an `execute_heartbeat` in
crates/bw-cli/src/commands/, dispatched like `status`. It needs no account, session or unlocked vault, so it belongs
with `Status` in the `Need::Nothing` arm of `Requires for Commands`. `tools.rs` already shows how a command
constructs a `bitwarden_core::Client` without logging in.

The SDK is a path dependency (`../sdk-internal`), so this builds against whatever the sdk-internal checkout holds.
Start only once that checkout contains {sdk-internal}'s verified commit; if `heartbeat` is missing from PlatformClient,
stop and report BLOCKED rather than adding it here.

Out of scope: `--response` JSON output, changes to other commands, the existing clippy and rustfmt warnings.
beads.acceptance:
- with no account or session configured, `cargo run -q -p bw-cli --bin bw -- heartbeat` exits 0 and prints one line that parses as an RFC 3339 date-time within 60 seconds of the current time
- `grep -rn "platform().heartbeat()" crates/bw-cli/src` finds the SDK call, and the heartbeat command code contains no `Utc::now` or `SystemTime::now`
- `bw heartbeat` is in the `Need::Nothing` arm of `Requires for Commands` in crates/bw-cli/src/main.rs
- crates/bw-cli/tests/integration_test.rs has a test running `bw heartbeat` that asserts exit 0 and an RFC 3339 line, and `cargo test -q --workspace` passes
